data.long_meaning: One who loves much, affectionate, loving. The name Muhibbun carries the meaning “Beloved” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the love of Allah (SWT) towards His creation and the love of the believer towards Allah and His Prophet (PBUH)
data.etymology: Muhibbun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Beloved.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muhibbun total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Muhibbun carries a rich cultural history in the Islamic world, as love and compassion are valued traits in Muslim societies. It implies a person who experiences deep emotions and displays kindness and care towards others. It is a dearly cherished name for boys in several Muslim communities, as they are encouraged to embody the qualities of love and compassion.
data.spiritual_significance: Muhibbun also holds immense spiritual significance in Islam as it is reminiscent of the divine love between Allah (God) and His creations. The name serves as a reminder to forever strive for closeness and connection to Allah. It also reflects the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) Sunan (traditions) and Sunnah (lifestyle) as he modeled love and kindness to his companions and the entire ummah (community). Embracing this name serves as an inspiration to cultivate a loving relationship with Allah and His creation, thus fulfilling one's spiritual and moral obligations.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Beloved" symbolizes One who loves much, affectionate, loving. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Muhibbun serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of beloved.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Muhibbun was a title given to the Sufi saint and scholar, Al-Ghazali. The name Muhibbun carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Ghazali was a prominent figure in Islamic scholarship and Sufism during the Middle Ages. He is known for his works on Islamic theology, philosophy, and law.
